crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit in Finance
children.blurb: An AI enablement audit in finance examines how an organization prepares, deploys, and oversees AI systems across financial operations, from credit decisioning and fraud detection to reporting and customer service.

children.name: Keeping Financial Data Out of Public Models
children.blurb: Keeping financial data out of public models concerns the controls, policies, and technical measures that prevent proprietary or regulated financial information from being used in training or fine-tuning publicly accessible AI models.

children.name: Model Risk and Bias Testing
children.blurb: Model risk and bias testing covers the formal review of quantitative models used in lending, pricing, fraud detection, capital allocation, and other financial decisions.

children.name: Mapping Financial AI to the Rules
children.blurb: This page maps where financial AI systems intersect with formal rules, including prudential regulation, securities law, anti-money laundering requirements, data protection, and contractual obligations.

children.name: Local and Air-Gapped Deployment
children.blurb: Local and air-gapped deployment means running AI models and supporting systems entirely on an organization's own hardware and network, with no connection to external cloud services or the public internet.

sections.body: In The AI Accountant, governance, risk and financial data security is the control layer around AI in accounting and finance. It covers how firms check that an AI tool is fit for a finance task, how they keep ledgers, payroll, tax and client data out of public models, how they test models for error and bias, how they map AI use to rules, and how they run systems locally when data cannot leave a controlled environment. In practice, AI is used to scan contracts and transactions, flag anomalies, draft control narratives, and compare policies against regulatory text. The work is not abstract policy. It is the daily review of prompts, data flows, access rights, model outputs, and audit trails. The aim is to make AI use explainable and defensible to auditors, regulators, and internal risk teams.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are relatively settled. Data classification and access control are mature disciplines, and teams can now keep sensitive financial data out of public models with private instances, redaction, and local deployment. Model risk and bias testing is less settled. Finance models often lack clear fairness labels, and bias can appear in credit, fraud, or expense decisions in ways that are hard to measure. Regulatory mapping is a moving target because rules differ by jurisdiction and change often, and the site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages as a sign of that volume. The honest limits are that no test proves a model is safe, no mapping stays current without maintenance, and local deployment trades some capability for control. Audits can show what was checked, but they cannot remove the need for human judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a sequence from permission to protection to proof. The AI Enablement Audit in Finance is the starting point for teams that need to review whether a tool, data flow, or vendor meets finance controls before wider use. Keeping Financial Data Out of Public Models then addresses the specific risk of leakage into external systems and the practical controls that reduce it. Model Risk and Bias Testing goes deeper into how outputs are challenged, documented, and monitored over time. Mapping Financial AI to the Rules connects those controls to regulatory expectations and helps readers find the relevant compliance material. Local and Air-Gapped Deployment covers the option for firms that cannot send data to a public cloud and need the model to run inside their own boundary. A reader would go to each page for a different layer of the same problem, and together they form a working reference for governance, risk, and financial data security.
